clue.text: 6 dn's family gets a cast-off

parts.note: the answer to 6 down is a venomous striker, a kind of serpent, so its family is the serpent's
kin are one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: A venomous creature's relatives receive a discarded garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 6 down, a cobra; a cobra's family is the snake's kin. A cast-off is something shed, as a snake sheds its outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent sloughs its outer covering regularly, so that shed covering is literally a thing cast off.

clue.text: This fur can, if I were to put it on

definitions.text: This fur can, if I were to put it on

parts.words: This fur can, if I were to put it on
parts.note: a whimsical reading: a speaker wearing this dark pelt would be capable, the fur's name heard as a contraction of 'is' followed by a synonym of can

explanation.surface: Someone muses on whether a fur coat would suit them.
explanation.walkthrough: A playful cryptic definition: the fur's name splits as S (a contracted 'is') plus ABLE, which means 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelt of a dark marten prized by furriers is one of the most luxurious furs.

clue.text: A coach I have will do for railing

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
contracted, I have becomes I've

explanation.surface: Someone says a coach of theirs will serve as a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railing' looks like a fence but is the adjective: scolding loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing at someone means scolding them with insults, so railing speech is insulting in nature.

clue.text: Shots fired through this doctor's in time, certainly

indicators.note: the doctor's degree goes inside the word for a period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification; the 's stands for 'is'
sure, as in 'sure!', means certainly

explanation.surface: A doctor arrives in time for something, certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: an opening in a castle wall through which guns are fired.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening in a parapet or fortification wall lets defenders fire guns outward.

clue.text: They could hardly be said to be commentators

definitions.text: They could hardly be said to be commentators

parts.words: They could hardly be said to be commentators
parts.note: split as 'common taters', commentators suggests ordinary potatoes, and this is a premium, royally named potato variety

explanation.surface: Some people are dismissed as poor pundits.
explanation.walkthrough: Taters is slang for potatoes; KING EDWARDS are a classic British potato variety, hardly 'common taters'.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known floury British potato variety named after a monarch, so not an ordinary spud.

clue.text: Nothing left in after rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up

explanation.surface: Nothing remains inside after prices go up.
explanation.definitionFit: A zero score, as in football results, means nothing at all.

clue.text: A pound extra on taxi for small party

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: A taxi fare carries a one-pound surcharge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra on' tells you the A and L come after the taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A small secret faction of plotters is a little group, a party in the political sense.

clue.text: The company, brother, takes on a venomous striker

explanation.surface: A firm's colleague signs up a dangerous attacking player.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded snake strikes at prey with a poisonous bite.

clue.text: One entitled to object to singular Times leader

parts.note: to bar something is to object to or forbid it
one is the singular number

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Times

explanation.surface: Someone with a title raises objections to a lone newspaper editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' looks like a newspaper editorial but only gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary titled rank just below a baron entitles its holder to be called Sir.

clue.text: Useless end of season in plain seaside resort

indicators.note: the useless thing and the letter go inside the word for a plain

parts.note: a llano is a grassy plain in South America
a dud is something useless

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of season

explanation.surface: A dull end to the holiday season on a flat landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: LLANDUDNO is a seaside resort in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian holiday town on the north Welsh coast is a classic seaside destination.

clue.text: Drink and a biscuit

definitions.meaning: a chocolate sandwich biscuit sold in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink with a biscuit on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOURBON biscuit is a familiar British chocolate cream biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a Kentucky whiskey and a chocolate cream cookie popular in Britain.

clue.text: Left part of Europe for part of Africa

parts.note: the peninsula of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone departs a European region for an African one.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African republic founded by freed American slaves is a country on that continent.

clue.text: Inevitable part for a showgirl

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the word Inevitable, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Being cast in a showgirl role was bound to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a stage role but signals a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva Perón began as a stage and radio actress before becoming Argentina's first lady, the subject of a musical.

clue.text: Linked up with each end in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Things joined together with every end left untidy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bound in chains is to be fastened or tied up, so linked up.

clue.text: Interdependence of officer, king and kinsman

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
R, for rex, stands for king
a relation is a kinsman

explanation.surface: Ties binding an officer, a monarch and a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that vary together are mutually connected, a mutual dependence.

clue.text: Old port for Borrow's Romany gentleman

definitions.meaning: a Sussex town, one of the ancient Cinque Ports
in George Borrow's book The Romany ... the Romany word for a gentleman

explanation.surface: An ancient harbour town and a character from a Victorian travel book.
explanation.walkthrough: RYE is an ancient port in Sussex; George Borrow wrote 'The Romany Rye', using the Romany word for gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a historic English harbour town and a Romany term for a gentleman.

clue.text: Maker of better parts in practice

definitions.meaning: running through roles improves actors' parts
a trial performance before the real thing

explanation.surface: Something that improves components is used in a workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks mechanical but means actors' roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-through before a play's opening polishes roles and is a practice session.

clue.text: Not called for or equipped to carry out a search?

definitions.text: or equipped to carry out a search?
definitions.meaning: police without a search warrant are not equipped to search

explanation.surface: Police arrive uninvited and without proper paperwork for a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word literally: lacking a warrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjustified conduct is uncalled-for, and literally the word describes officers holding no search warrant.

clue.text: Our daily bursting into song it's wormwood!

indicators.note: the jumbled newspaper goes inside the song

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song

indicators.note: bursting means the letters of the newspaper are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the setter's own daily paper is The Times

explanation.surface: A newspaper suddenly breaks into song about a bitter herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our daily' is the paper the clue appears in, the Times; 'bursting' scrambles it (giving TEMIS) and 'into' places it within the song.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood is a bitter herb of a plant genus named after the Greek goddess Artemis.

clue.text: Restriction of freedom makes MPs stop…

parts.note: MPs sit in the House of Commons
to arrest is to stop or halt

explanation.surface: Something forces members of Parliament to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 19 across, where proroguing Parliament is what makes MPs stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Confinement to one's home by authority is a curb on liberty.

clue.text: "Some blessed Hope, whereof he knew And I was ." (Hardy)

definitions.text: "Some blessed Hope, whereof he knew And I was ." (Hardy)

parts.words: "Some blessed Hope, whereof he knew And I was ." (Hardy)
parts.note: the closing lines of Thomas Hardy's poem The Darkling Thrush, with the final word missing

explanation.surface: A quotation from a poem with its last word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the gap from Hardy's 'The Darkling Thrush': the bird knew of hope, the poet did not.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet did not know of the hope the bird sang of, so he was ignorant of it.

clue.text: … for this rogue means to do just that

definitions.text: this rogue means to do just that
definitions.meaning: put before rogue it makes prorogue, which means to suspend Parliament, the MPs' stop from 17 across

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a scoundrel intends to do exactly that.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO + ROGUE gives PROROGUE, to suspend a session of Parliament, which makes MPs stop as in 17 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons.

clue.text: Intent to get postal order in place of cash

indicators.note: the order goes inside the place where money is kept

parts.note: a purse is where cash is kept
PO is a postal order, a British money order bought at a post office

explanation.surface: Someone means to obtain a money order instead of using cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place of' reads as 'instead of', but 'in' puts PO into PURSE, the place of cash. A postal order is a British money order.
explanation.definitionFit: A purpose is an aim or intention, what one means to do.

clue.text: A twisted 24 with a painless feeling

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of 24 across are wrung into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 24 across, impressive work

explanation.surface: A distorted feeling without pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' scrambles the answer to 24 across (giving NALGESI); the clue's two As go either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the absence of sensitivity to pain, a numb state.

clue.text: In dividing 25, gets more

indicators.note: the word In splits the answer to 25 down in two

parts.note: the answer to 25 down, meaningless conversation

explanation.surface: Splitting something, one obtains extra.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire extra of something is to add to one's holdings.

clue.text: Name of famous traveller bringing no stuff back

indicators.note: back means the letters of both words are read in reverse

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing
to cram is to stuff

explanation.surface: An explorer comes home with no luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: Marco Polo was the Venetian who travelled to China.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian explorer who reached Kublai Khan's court was called Marco Polo, so this is his first name.

clue.text: Jock's sorry about the paint

parts.note: och is a Scottish exclamation of regret; Jock is a nickname for a Scot
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A Scotsman apologises over the painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used in painting.

clue.text: Impressive work sounds as if it's over one's head

indicators.note: says the words describe something that is pronounced the same as the answer

parts.note: the ceiling is overhead in a room

explanation.surface: Something remarkable seems too clever to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressive' means stamping an impression, as with a wax seal; 'over one's head' looks like 'too hard to grasp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamping wax with a signet makes an impression, so it is work that impresses.

clue.text: Meaningless conversation tapped?

definitions.meaning: a fuel supplied by mains and drawn off from a pipe

explanation.surface: Idle chatter that might be bugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tapped' suggests a bugged phone call, but the fuel is what is tapped from the mains.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both idle chatter and a fuel drawn from pipes.

clue.text: Truly old-fashioned

parts.note: an archaic phrase meaning truly, from the old word sooth for truth

explanation.surface: Something genuinely antique.
explanation.definitionFit: Sooth is an archaic word for truth, so the phrase is a dated way of saying indeed.

clue.text: Deposit of dust is smaller-nothing in it!

indicators.note: the nothing goes inside the word for smaller

parts.note: less means smaller
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A deposit of dust is shrinking, with nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is fine windblown silt laid down as a sediment.

clue.text: She's alien, possibly of Aryan extraction

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A woman is a foreigner, perhaps of distant ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: The majority people of Sri Lanka descend from Indo-Aryan settlers from northern India.
